items: Fixes: nameplates on name-only plates, the group gear check and your own inspect window, item goals counted on every character, and the upgrade notice putting on the right copy.
Polish: several upgrades looted at once wait their turn, a notice goes once the item is worn, and a goal already reached says so when you set it.
Loot an upgrade and a notice offers to put it on; for a ring or a trinket you choose which one it replaces.
Milestones: your 1,000th kill, 100th quest, first boss and more get a short notice, and a list on the stats page.
Boss guide: when you target or pull a boss, its abilities from the dungeon journal show under your boss note.
Roll advice: the loot roll window lights the button to press and says why - Need for a wish or an upgrade, Pass for gear you can't use.
A group gear check: /fgui gear lists everyone in your group with their item level, the lowest first, and the group's average.
Lifetime stats: /fgui stats gives totals for this character and all of them - time played, quests, kills, gold, loot, bosses and runs.
Our own nameplates: the health bar is the add-on's, on a black backing, with the level in its color beside the name.
One record of best times: the boss timer's new-best lines now agree with your run log, which also keeps how long each boss fight took.
A loot wishlist: click an item in the loot browser to star it, and you are told when it drops, comes up in a roll, or a boss that drops it is your target. /fgui wish lists them.
Point at a boss: its tooltip lists what it drops that you want or that would be an upgrade for you.
Quest mobs: nameplates mark the mobs you still need for a quest, with how many are left.
Starcut windows and tooltips: their corners cut with a fine rim, and stars on big windows.
Lighter: the add-on does less while you play, in and out of a fight.
Farming: the first two minutes show what you have made so far, not a guess at an hour; right-click the whose-upgrade list to put it away.
Starcut reaches the rest of the screen: action buttons and bag slots are cut like gems, their cooldowns to match, and the minimap can be a diamond (Features tab).
Whose upgrade: in a group, a boss drop shows whose upgrade it is, and by how much, among players with the add-on - before anyone rolls.
A run log: /fgui runs keeps your dungeon and raid times, kills, wipes, deaths and loot, with a best time for each place.
Farming by zone: /fgui farm zones lists your best farming spots by gold an hour, and whether your latest time there was up or down.
Goals: gold on all your characters, a level and a mount join the goals panel; an item counts on every character and says where it drops.
Nameplates: the threat color is on the plate's edge too, so a tank sees which mob is slipping.
Starcut reaches every bar: your cast bar, the class resource (its dots become small diamonds), raid frames, nameplates, timers, experience and totems.
Screenshot mode: /fgui showcase fills every frame with a picture-worthy sample (a boss with a breath on its way, a party of four) and clears the screen of everything else.
A loot browser: /fgui drops lists what each boss dropped while you were there, raid by raid, with the upgrades for you first.
A threat meter of its own: in a group, who has how much threat on your target, and a warning color as you near the top.
Farming sessions: /fgui farm shows the time and what you make an hour, in gold and in loot, and each session counts in your weekly recap.
Gear sets: the set you wear is named over your player frame, /fgui set <name> puts one on, and the first five sets can have keys.
A new look for your unit frames, Starcut: bars cut to points that glow in their own color, a diamond portrait with stars on its points, and the name above the bars.
Prefer the box? Look tab, Frame style: Classic brings it back at once.
Open windows do far less work: the character window, vendor, mailbox, auction house, collections and every scrolling list are looked over more cheaply while they are open.

A login briefing: a few seconds after you log in, one small window says what is waiting: crafts ready, mail on your other characters, lockouts reset, rested experience, jobs left. /fgui briefing shows it again.
Skill-ups on the profession window: the recipes that still give skill points, best first, with what each needs.
Your weekly recap: what each character did last week, gold, time, levels, raids and best loot (/fgui recap).
Celestial themes take the place of Runic: 38 night skies with twinkling stars, constellations and shooting stars. A Runic theme you use becomes the Celestial one made from it.
The minimap is a star chart on Celestial themes, with the sun or moon by the game's clock; and twelve more accent colors, 31 in all.
An Interface size slider beside Text size on the Layout tab, and /fgui uisize and /fgui textsize.
Polish: tooltips on the option buttons and size sliders, the new tools in the Tools menu and as key bindings, and long list lines shown in full under the mouse.
The whole add-on polished, file by file: everything it shows is translated, every message is a full sentence, and commands say what they did or why not.
